title: SAFER Act of 2017
official_summary:
Sexual Assault Forensic Evidence Reporting Act of 2017 or the SAFER Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the DNA Sexual Assault Justice Act of 2004 to require the Department of Justice (DOJ), in providing information about the role of forensic nurses to certain health-related entities, to provide information about the role of both adult and pediatric forensic nurses. DOJ must also provide additional information on the need for pediatric sexual assault nurse examiners in responding to the abuse of both children and adolescents.

(Sec. 3) Additionally, the bill amends the DNA Analysis Backlog Elimination Act of 2000 to reauthorize through FY2022 the requirement for DOJ to allocate a certain percentage of funds under the Debbie Smith DNA Backlog Grant Program for grants to audit backlogged sexual assault kits (i.e., rape kits).

It extends from 2018 to 2023 the sunset date of DOJ's authority to award grants to collect DNA of arrestees and to audit backlogged rape kits.

summary.headline: A 2018 law updates federal rules on forensic nurses for sexual assault cases and extends federal funding for testing backlogged rape kits.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Justice to share information about both adult and pediatric forensic nurses with certain health-related groups. It also explains the need for pediatric sexual assault nurse examiners when children and teens are abused. The law extends the Debbie Smith DNA Backlog Grant Program so that a set share of its funds goes to audit backlogged sexual assault kits through fiscal year 2022. It also moves the program's sunset date from 2018 to 2023 for DOJ's authority to award grants for collecting DNA from arrestees and auditing rape kits.

who_it_affects.group: Forensic nurses and sexual assault nurse examiners
who_it_affects.how: The Justice Department must provide information about their role, including pediatric examiners who treat children and adolescents.

who_it_affects.group: Hospitals and health-related entities that treat sexual assault victims
who_it_affects.how: They receive DOJ information about adult and pediatric forensic nurses and the need for pediatric examiners.

who_it_affects.group: Crime labs and local law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: They may receive federal grant money to audit backlogged sexual assault kits, since that funding is extended through fiscal year 2022.
Their untested rape kits may be audited sooner because federal backlog funding continues longer.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 8, 2018; the backlog audit funding requirement runs through fiscal year 2022, and the grant authority sunset date is extended to 2023.
